items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: So they had a sign out there, Art Hodes needs Columbia Five feature in the King of the Tailgate, George Brunus.

ctx.x: I was playing with Hodes at, I didn't know what it was all about. I'm playing with Hodes up at the Childs. Yeah. So they had a sign out there, Art Hodes needs Columbia Five feature in the King of the Tailgate, George Brunus. So I said to myself, what is this King of the Tailgate? What is this tailgate? So a guy come in and explain it to me. Why did they, because you sit on the tailgate of the wagon, you can't, you need more room to slide the slide. That's the way they do it. They set the drums up in front and…
Yeah. But you've never had that term applied to you down in New Orleans?

items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: We called it the Art Hodes Columbia Quintet, featuring Rod Kless and George Brunis and we also -- the three of us split the money.

ctx.x: Childe's, was that like a cafeteria?

That was a cafeteria, and this was 1940. I'd been in New York practically two years, and so I said, sure. He says, okay, who would you like to have? I says, well, I'd like to have George Brunis who's available, I'd like to have Rod Cless. I don't know who I can get on drums. It turned out we got Joe Grasso. And on trumpet, I couldn't get Marty Marsala, he wasn't available. And I didn't know about experience. I never had one yet. I hadn't felt that scene yet.
